Messages.Author: KButter940
Messages.Body:
Some friends convinced me that I should try out this game. I didn't want
to get involved in it, because I knew that I'd get too involved in it, and
spend too much money on it.

Anyhow, now I'm involved, and I find myself reading this newsgroup
everyday, looking for new bits of wisdom. And I have some questions....

If I press to continue combat, do we have to re-establish range, or do we
continue at whatever range we established earlier. That is, if we played
the last round at long range, do we start the new round at long range, or
at close range?

My friends gave me tons of commons and vampires. I'm missing maybe fifteen
vampires, and have a pretty good selection of most commons. Do you think
I'm better off buying boxes of boosters, or just identifying the cool
uncommons and rares I need, and buying them individually off of here?

Someone, (I think it was Alan Kwan), wrote that he'd always play sudden
reversal whenever someone tried to give Protean to a non-gangrel, or
dominance to a gangrel, which suggested to me that this would make a very
powerful combination. (I'm guessing that the idea is that you could have
very powerful bleeders, who can send to torpor anyone that blocks them).
Do you think it works better to give dominance to gangrels, or protean to
another clan, and if so, what other clan? I sort of like the idea of a
Ventrue deck with lots of protean skill cards, because it seems like you
could do well with bleeding, combat and voting. Would it work better with
a mixed clan deck (some Protean, some Dominance, and Gangrels and
Ventrue)?

I like the idea of sending a blocker right to the ash heap. As I
understand it, you have to do x+2 points of aggravated damage, where x is
the blockers current blood. What combinations of cards will do this? Will
say, Cauldron of Blood and Claws do this?

Thanks,
Lee

Messages.Author: Stephen Beaulieu
Messages.Body:
In article <43v6ht$b...@newsbf02.news.aol.com>, kbutt...@aol.com
(KButter940) wrote:

: If I press to continue combat, do we have to re-establish range, or do we

: continue at whatever range we established earlier. That is, if we played
: the last round at long range, do we start the new round at long range, or
: at close range?

Each round of combat starts at close range. So if you press to continue
combat, the next round is at close range regardless of the range of the
last round.

: Someone, (I think it was Alan Kwan), wrote that he'd always play sudden

: reversal whenever someone tried to give Protean to a non-gangrel, or
: dominance to a gangrel, which suggested to me that this would make a very
: powerful combination. (I'm guessing that the idea is that you could have
: very powerful bleeders, who can send to torpor anyone that blocks them).
: Do you think it works better to give dominance to gangrels, or protean to
: another clan, and if so, what other clan? I sort of like the idea of a
: Ventrue deck with lots of protean skill cards, because it seems like you
: could do well with bleeding, combat and voting. Would it work better with
: a mixed clan deck (some Protean, some Dominance, and Gangrels and
: Ventrue)?

I think it is very tough to add a new skill to an entire clan of vamps.
You are dependant on a lot of skill cards instead of other useful masters,
and it is slow getting the right combination of skills on a vamp. I
prefer to mix clans (usually two clans to a deck) that combine the facets
I am looking for, when possible. But that's just me, and you can't always
work it that way. If I had to choose between giving dominate to Gangrels
or Protean to Ventrue, i would choose the ventrue deck, but that is also
just my style of play. I don't do so well with Gangrel decks.

: I like the idea of sending a blocker right to the ash heap. As I

: understand it, you have to do x+2 points of aggravated damage, where x is
: the blockers current blood. What combinations of cards will do this? Will
: say, Cauldron of Blood and Claws do this?

This combination will not work as Claws only make hand damage aggravated,
and Cauldron of Blood is not hand damage. Combinations that can cause
this are: Dragon Breath rounds and guns, Basilia and a heavy potence
attack, the Sengir Dagger and a heavy potence attack, Flamethrowers, Burst
of Sunlight, Walk of Flame, Body of Sun, and heavy potence Claws. There
are probably a couple more, but I can't think of them off the top of my
head.

Welcome to one of the best games around.

: Thanks,
: Lee

I hope this helps

stephen

Messages.Author: Alan Kwan
Messages.Body:
In article <43v6ht$b...@newsbf02.news.aol.com> kbutt...@aol.com (KButter940) writes:

>If I press to continue combat, do we have to re-establish range, or do we
>continue at whatever range we established earlier. That is, if we played
>the last round at long range, do we start the new round at long range, or
>at close range?

At close range.

>Someone, (I think it was Alan Kwan), wrote that he'd always play sudden
>reversal whenever someone tried to give Protean to a non-gangrel, or
>dominance to a gangrel,

Yes, that was me.

> which suggested to me that this would make a very
>powerful combination. (I'm guessing that the idea is that you could have
>very powerful bleeders, who can send to torpor anyone that blocks them).

It is a moderately powerful combination. The reason that I'll play
Sudden Reversal against Skill cards is not because of the power of
the combo, but because such a deck would suffer miserably if the
Skill masters get S. Reversed. More specifically, the hand jams.
Soon he'll be like playing with a 1-card hand instead of a 7-card
hand. Noticed my reference to the Barrens there?

Please refer to more theory-orientated articles published by Curt Adams
and me. To see what I'm talking about, try building such deck and
do an experimental session, assuming that all the skill cards
get SR'ed. (Stop when you begin to fall asleep.)

>Do you think it works better to give dominance to gangrels, or protean to
>another clan, and if so, what other clan? I sort of like the idea of a
>Ventrue deck with lots of protean skill cards, because it seems like you
>could do well with bleeding, combat and voting. Would it work better with
>a mixed clan deck (some Protean, some Dominance, and Gangrels and
>Ventrue)?

I'm not sure, but I think it's better to use a mixed clan deck
and put in half-half skill cards than to use all one clan and add
the `unnatural' skill card. The deck is less suspectible to
jamming this way, because getting skills printed on vampires
is more reliable than getting it through your Masters.

>I like the idea of sending a blocker right to the ash heap. As I
>understand it, you have to do x+2 points of aggravated damage, where x is
>the blockers current blood. What combinations of cards will do this? Will
>say, Cauldron of Blood and Claws do this?

No. Cauldron of Blood is not a Hand strike, so Claws don't apply.
Growing Fury and Claws would do it, for example.

Don't worry too much about burning vampires; if you can always
torporize blockers, that's good enough.

--
"Live Life with Heart."

Alan Kwan kw...@cs.cornell.edu

Messages.Author: Biomech8
Messages.Body:
LEE: If I press to continue combat, do we have to re-establish range, or

do we
continue at whatever range we established earlier.

BIOMECHANOID: Re-establish range (starting at close)
LEE: Do you think I'm better off buying boxes of boosters, or just

identifying the cool
uncommons and rares I need, and buying them individually off of here?

BIOMECHANOID: If you just want one deck I would suggest buying individual
cards, if you want more than one deck or you want to try for a complete
set I would stick to the boosters and maybe buy some hard to get cards.
LEE: Do you think it works better to give dominance to gangrels, or

protean to
another clan, and if so, what other clan?

BIOMECHANOID: The Malkavians already have someone with Dom. and Prot.
(Zebulon) and I would suggest playing a mix of clans other than just one.
Don't forget to watch out for Gangrel De-Evolutions.
LEE: I sort of like the idea of a Ventrue deck with lots of protean skill

cards, because it seems like you could do well with bleeding, combat and
voting. Would it work better with
a mixed clan deck (some Protean, some Dominance, and Gangrels and
Ventrue)?

BIOMECHANOID: I think that would be covering too many aspects at one
time. You might end up with all vote cards while in combat, all combat
cards when you want to bleed etc. It is not impossible though, just more
difficult. Though single aspect decks have their weaknesses too.
LEE: I like the idea of sending a blocker right to the ash heap (so do I
-BM). As I

understand it, you have to do x+2 points of aggravated damage, where x is
the blockers current blood. What combinations of cards will do this? Will
say, Cauldron of Blood and Claws do this?

BIOMECHANOID: Cauldron of blood is not hand damage so it won't work, but
lucky blow and any of the increase hand damage cards from the potence
discipline work nicely. I think this game is the best one out there, and
I suggest you play it ranks far above the rest.

In article <hippo-22099...@gill.hrc.utexas.edu> hi...@mail.utexas.edu (Stephen Beaulieu) writes:

>I think it is very tough to add a new skill to an entire clan of vamps.
>You are dependant on a lot of skill cards instead of other useful masters,
>and it is slow getting the right combination of skills on a vamp. I
>prefer to mix clans (usually two clans to a deck) that combine the facets
>I am looking for, when possible. But that's just me, and you can't always
>work it that way.

I'd do the same too; I think that's better than relying solely on skill
cards, because if you don't draw one or they gets SR'ed, my hand
jams.

However, one-clan decks are in general far better, because you can
use large vampires with good skills and use Minion Taps and Blood
Dolls. That's more `economic' than Master Skill cards.

>If I had to choose between giving dominate to Gangrels
>or Protean to Ventrue, i would choose the ventrue deck, but that is also
>just my style of play. I don't do so well with Gangrel decks.

Because, as I stated before, Gangrels don't fight as good as
Brujah. Protean Claws are not IMO as flexible as Potence. The
real strength of Protean lies in the untap spoilers, but Gangrel
hasn't got good actions to exploit that with, since Army of Rats
has been ruled non-cumulative.

Messages.Author: Alan Kwan
Messages.Body:
Would anyone be interested in trying out this variation?

Army of Rats
Animalism
Action, Undirected, +1 stealth

If successful, the Army of Rats is in play. During your untap each
round, your prey loses 1 pool for each Army of Rats you have in play.
Any minion can burn all Army of Rats you have in play with a
Directed action.

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
Alan Kwan writes:
>Because, as I stated before, Gangrels don't fight as good as
>Brujah. Protean Claws are not IMO as flexible as Potence. The
>real strength of Protean lies in the untap spoilers, but Gangrel
>hasn't got good actions to exploit that with, since Army of Rats
>has been ruled non-cumulative.

Actually Protean has quite a variety of nice non-strike cards, such as
Form of the Ghost or Gleam of Red Eyes; Protean only makes a fairly
respectable mono-discipline combat (only Celerity is better). Brujah have
access to better comparisons, but not through Potence.

Personally I think Potence is one of the weakest disciplines as it hasn't

much variety - it's mostly strikes and presses (often to continue), and
those are of dubious value in a discipline without any good way to prevent
damage.

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

Messages.Author: James R. McClure Jr.
Messages.Body:

Peace Andrew,

Well Nosf get no respect because they are a weak clan in Jyhad. As far as
the Spawning Pool is concerned: if you prey isn't a bleeder, well, there
isn't much you can do about it; make sure you have enough intercept (Raven
Spies) to stop most bleeds; make sure you have some presses (Mighty Grapple,
Thrown Sewer Lid [sup], Aid from Bats [sup]) to assure a second round. Your
prey will be hesitent to bleed you if you have 4+ blood on tSP and you really
can't _force_ him/her/it to bleed you.
